pictures.scene: Briton Riviere, Daniel's Answer to the King — the floor of a stone pit under the palace, one tall old man standing alone against the dark with his hands bound behind his back, his head thrown right back and his face lifted up into a shaft of light that falls from somewhere above and out of the picture, his white hair and his lined throat and cheek taking all of it, a long dark blue Babylonian robe falling straight to his bare feet with a broad gold worked belt at the waist and a gold collar at the neck, the wall behind him black in the corner and running away into worked brickwork at the right with a band of blue and red glazed rosettes along the top, a great lioness pacing in out of the shadow at his side with her head lowered and her pale eyes fixed on him, a second lion's heavy flank showing at the edge beyond her, and in front of them a broad pale stone pavement cracked and lit, with gnawed bones and a torn skull scattered across it, they will put you out of the synagogues, anyone who kills you will think he is offering a service to God, …
pictures.name: pd_riviere_daniel_answer

pictures.scene: Camille Corot, The Road to Sevres — a broad pale country road climbing over the brow of a hill and running away down into a wide hazy valley, one small solitary woman walking off down it with her back turned, a white cap on her head, a dark cloak over a red bodice and a long skirt, a white bundle carried on her hip and her shadow laid out behind her on the sand, a great mass of dark green trees falling down the whole right side of the picture from the top corner, their leaves worked in flicks of blue green and grey, a slender lit poplar standing up at the left over a low wall and the pale gables of a village, a strip of green pasture with two small cows beyond them, the far country opening out grey and gold toward a distant town on the skyline, a soft blue sky over the upper half with long banks of cream and grey cloud drawn across it, and the worked road filling the whole bottom of the picture in warm pink and lilac with the ruts and stones showing, now, however, i am going to him who sent me, yet none of you asks me, where are you going, …
pictures.name: pd_corot_road

pictures.scene: Vincent van Gogh, Sorrowing Old Man — one old working man sitting alone on a plain rush seated chair in the corner of a bare room, bent right forward over his knees with his elbows on them and both fists pressed hard against his eyes so that his face is hidden in his own hands, his bald head and thin yellow white hair blazing against the pale wall, a worn blue working suit buttoned to the throat with the sleeves and knees creased in long strokes of lighter blue, heavy brown laced boots set flat on the boards with the worn soles and nails showing, the chair painted in strong red brown with its back and stretchers worked in thick lines, the floor running away under him in long streaks of gold, orange and green, a plain pale wall behind with a white sill and a dark iron fireplace at the left, and a second chair showing at the right edge, instead, your hearts are filled with sorrow because i have told you these things, …
pictures.name: pd_van_gogh_sorrowing_old_man

pictures.scene: John Martin, Belshazzar's Feast — an enormous torchlit banqueting court in Babylon seen from above the table, in the middle of it one prophet standing alone in a long dark robe with his grey head bare and his arm flung straight out, pointing up and away at the writing that has broken out in light on the wall, all round him the king's guests thrown into confusion, women in white and rose gowns falling back from the table with their arms thrown up and their faces turned to the light, men in crimson and blue cowering along the near side, a long white damask cloth running right across the bottom of the picture covered with gold dishes, goblets, ewers and heaped fruit with a deep red carpet hanging below it, dark robed figures crowding in at the lower left corner, a fire burning on an altar at the left with a procession of tiny torchbearers climbing a great stair beyond it, tier upon tier of worked tan columns, carved friezes and terraces running back into the distance packed with hundreds of small figures, and above the roofline a huge tiered tower standing pale against a black rolling storm of smoke and cloud, he will convict the world in regard to sin and righteousness and judgment, …
pictures.name: pd_john_martin_belshazzars_feast

pictures.scene: Bartolome Bermejo, Saint Michael Triumphant over the Devil — a tall archangel standing full height against a burnished gold ground, his whole body sheathed in polished gilt plate armour worked with foliage and set with pearls and rubies, dark mail showing at the throat, the elbows and the thighs, a brilliant crimson silk mantle lined with gold brocade billowing out behind him across the whole upper left of the picture, great wings of gold, orange and red feathers spread open on either side of his head, his face young and calm with the eyes lowered toward the thing under his feet, fair hair curling to his shoulders, both hands lifted, the right one gripping the long sword raised to strike and running up out of the top corner of the picture, the left holding a round crystal and gold shield before him, his pointed gilt sabatons set hard on a scaled black and gold dragon sprawled over the whole bottom of the picture, its red eyes glaring, its jaws open full of teeth and its clawed feet thrown out across the earth, and kneeling at the left a donor in a tall black cap and a silver grey damask robe with an open book held in both hands, looking up at him, and in regard to judgment, because the prince of this world has been condemned, …
pictures.name: pd_bermejo_saint_michael_triumphant_over_the_devil

pictures.scene: Juan Bautista Maino, Pentecost — a white dove hanging open winged in the middle of a blaze of gold light at the top of the picture, a ring of pale blue round it and long shafts of light breaking down from it on every side through banks of grey and brown cloud, small tongues of red flame scattered all down the air and one of them burning over the head of each person below, cherub heads looking out of the cloud in both upper corners, and under it a crowded company packed shoulder to shoulder, Mary seated in the middle in a deep blue mantle over a rose pink gown with a pale veil over her hair, her face lifted and both hands opened, an old bald apostle in an orange red cloak behind her lifting a finger toward the light, a grey bearded man in a dull orange mantle beside him, a young apostle in a green tunic under a scarlet cloak at the right with his head thrown back, more faces crowded behind them with hands raised and fingers pointing up, a young woman kneeling in the front in a white gown under a great golden yellow mantle with her long hair loose down her back and both hands crossed on her breast, a deep rose cloth fallen over the step, and a pale grey stone floor running across the bottom of the picture, when the spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all truth, …
pictures.name: pd_maino_volken

pictures.scene: Cefalu Cathedral, Christ Pantocrator — an enormous half length figure of Christ set in gold mosaic in the curve of an apse, His face filling the middle of the picture with great dark eyes looking straight out, long brown hair parted and falling in worked waves over both shoulders, a full dark beard and a long thin nose, a cross set with blue and green stones worked into the gold halo behind His head, a deep blue mantle wrapped over an olive gold tunic with the folds drawn in long gold lines, His right hand lifted at the left edge of the picture with the fingers opened in blessing, His left holding a great open book up before Him with Greek and Latin letters set into the white pages, bands of worked ornament running round the arch above and below Him in blue, red and gold, and beneath that a lower register on a gold ground with the Virgin standing in a dark blue mantle with both hands raised and a tall haloed archangel in jewelled court dress and dark folded wings on either side of her, he will glorify me by taking from what is mine and disclosing it to you, …
pictures.name: pd_master_of_cefalu_christ_pantocrator

pictures.scene: Annibale Carracci, The Holy Women at the Tomb — two tall women standing close together on broken ground outside a dark rock, the first full length in a deep blue mantle drawn right over her head and falling to her bare feet, a brilliant vermilion gown under it belted at the waist, her face turned in three quarter view with the mouth open, one hand thrown up open palmed beside her head and the other laid flat on her breast, the second woman swinging round in front of her with her back half turned, a white head cloth bound over her hair, a great pale grey white mantle over a dark green gown spread across the whole lower middle of the picture in heavy folds, a gold sleeve showing at her elbow and one bare sandalled foot set out on the earth, her hand reaching back empty toward the other, a third woman in yellow and crimson crowded in at the right edge of the picture with a hand showing below, dark leaves and a rough brown cliff filling the upper right, a strip of pale dawn sky and a dim far country at the left with two tiny riders, and bare worked earth with a tuft of grass across the bottom, in a little while you will see me no more, and then after a little while you will see me, …
pictures.name: pd_carracci_holy_women_at_the_tomb

pictures.scene: Heinrich Hofmann, Christ and the Rich Young Ruler — two figures close up against a dim grey stone wall with a faint warm glow standing behind one head, at the left Christ turned a little toward us with His face fully lit, long brown hair falling past His shoulders, a short beard, and the eyes steady and sad as He looks away past the other man, a dull red brown robe open at the throat with the sleeve full to the wrist and a heavy dark blue green mantle hanging over His left shoulder and down the whole side of the picture, His right arm reaching across and out of the left edge with the hand opened and the fingers spread, at the right a young man standing half turned away with his head bent and his eyes lowered, a tall silk turban wound about his dark curls with a jewelled clasp set in the front, a sea green sleeved robe belted with a worked sash, a long cream silk mantle bordered with gold thrown over his shoulder and falling to the bottom of the picture, and both his hands drawn in and clasped quietly before him, we do not understand what he is saying, …
pictures.name: pd_hofmann_christ_and_the_rich_young_ruler

pictures.scene: Berthe Morisot, The Cradle — a young mother sitting close beside a draped cradle in a quiet room, seen in profile at the left with her head bent and her cheek resting on her bent hand, her dark hair gathered up with a little bow, a black ribbon at her throat, a dark blue grey jacket over a white frilled chemise, and her eyes lowered and fixed through the gauze on the child, the whole right side of the picture taken up by the hanging of the cradle, a great sweep of thin white muslin caught up at the top with a pink ribbon and falling in long soft folds over everything, and behind it the baby lying asleep on its back with its small pink face turned up, one fist thrown out on the bedding, the white quilt of the cradle spread across the whole bottom of the picture worked in cream and grey with fine craquelure running over it, a pale curtain filling the upper left and a strip of dark wall showing between them, she forgets her anguish because of her joy that a child has been born into the world, …
pictures.name: pd_morisot_the_cradle

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Peasant Wedding — a wedding feast in a barn, the bride sitting still in the middle behind the table with her hands folded, her eyes closed and a small smile on her face, her long red brown hair loose, a dark green gown and a paper crown hung on the green cloth pinned to the wall above her head, guests packed along the table on either side in white caps, black caps, red and green hoods, one old man drinking from a brown jug, another tipping a bowl to his mouth, a woman in a white headcloth passing a cup, a man in a red cap and a long olive coat leaning right across the boards to set down the dishes, in front of them two servers carrying a door laid flat as a tray heaped with white bowls of custard, the nearest one swung round with his back to us in a bright blue jacket, a long white apron, green stockings and black shoes, a red cap with white ties on his head and both hands gripping the pole, straw and a worked tan wall running right across the top of the picture with a dark beam in the corner, and the bare earth floor of the barn filling the bottom crossed by boots and the legs of the table, your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_peasant_wedding

pictures.scene: Jan Victors, Hannah Praying in the Temple — one very old woman seen close up from the waist, her whole face lifted and lit, the eyes turned up and away past us, the mouth a little open as though she were still speaking, every line and fold of the aged cheek, throat and brow worked out in warm light, a wide pleated hat of orange and dark red set back on her head with a long dark veil falling from under it down both sides of her body, a heavy fur banded gown over a red brown sleeved robe with wide gold embroidered cuffs at the wrists, a full white gathered collar drawn close at the neck with a small gold clasp below it, and both hands brought together in the middle of the picture and tightly interlaced, the knuckles and veins catching the light against the black of her bodice, the temple behind her in dim grey and brown with a dark railing and a tall pier at the left and a pale stone column base at the right, ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete, …
pictures.name: pd_victors_hanna_biddend_in_de_tempel

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Jacob Blessing the Sons of Joseph — a very old father propped up in his bed at the left in a loose white shirt with the full sleeve falling back from the wrist, his white hair under a pale gold cap, his hollow face bent down with the eyes nearly shut, and his right hand laid flat and open on the fair head of the smaller boy while his other hand is held gently aside, a young man in a great cream turban standing close behind him with a dark red brown robe and a quiet half smiling face, steadying the old arm as it reaches across, two children leaning in over the bedside below, the fair one with his eyes closed and both hands folded on his breast under the blessing, the dark haired one beside him looking straight out at us, a mother at the right in a deep brown gown with a gold chain, a jewelled band in her hair and a white collar, her hands resting on the bed as she watches, a worked grey and brown wall and a dark hanging filling the upper third, and a great deep red coverlet spread across the whole bottom of the picture with a gold tassel lying on it, for the father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that i came from god, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_jacob_blessing_the_sons_of_joseph

pictures.scene: Thomas Cole, The Departure — a wide green valley in the morning with a company riding out from home, a great towered castle of warm brown stone standing on the wooded height at the right with a white keep and a flag lifted above it, a long arched aqueduct running away to the left along the cliff, blue mountains with a sharp peak and a thin white waterfall behind it, a pale blue sky over the upper third worked with long banks of cream and grey cloud, below the castle a gatehouse tower on a low stone bridge with a crimson and gold banner flying from it, and out of the arch a troop of riders coming down and away over the bridge in scarlet, blue and white with lances and bows carried up, the dark masses of great oaks spreading across the whole middle of the picture, a sunlit sward of grass falling to the front with goats lying under a leaning tree, a stream running out below the bridge among rocks and reeds, and in the foreground one old hermit in a worn brown habit standing alone on the path with a staff in his hand and the other hand lifted after them, i came from the father and entered the world, in turn, i will leave the world and go to the father, …
pictures.name: pd_cole_the_departure

pictures.scene: Duccio, Christ and the Samaritan Woman — two figures standing and sitting on either side of a well on a worn burnished gold ground that fills the whole upper part of the picture, scratched and abraded so the red underlayer shows through it in long streaks, at the left Christ seated on the low parapet in a deep blue mantle over a red brown robe with a fine gold border, a scored gold halo behind His brown hair, His face turned up toward her with the lips parted as He speaks and His right hand lifted open before Him while the other rests on the rim, His bare feet set on the pale stone step below, the well itself built up in the middle in green marble panels framed with white stone, hexagonal and brimming, at the right a woman standing full length in a long cream gown falling in close folds to the ground, a white head cloth wound about her head and throat with a round red clay jar balanced on top of it, one hand raised toward Him in surprise and the other holding a roped bucket at her side, a dark cloak and sleeve of an off frame figure showing at the left edge, and a pale wall at the right, because of this, we believe that you came from god, …
pictures.name: pd_duccio_christ_and_the_samaritan_woman

pictures.scene: Ludolf Bakhuizen, Christ in the Storm on the Sea of Galilee — one small open fishing boat driven over a wild sea under a black storm, the whole upper half of the picture a near solid dark worked with drifting smoke coloured cloud and long streaks of rain falling across it, a huge white foaming breaker rearing up on the left and bursting into spray along the whole side of the boat, the little mast raking across the picture with a torn pennant at its head and a tangle of loose rigging blown out sideways, the cream sail half brailed and bellying out full in the wind, one bare headed man clinging to the mast and hauling on the canvas, another hunched over the gunwale behind him, and in the bottom of the boat a close huddle of frightened men, a white bearded one in a blue coat flinging out his hand, a man in a red cap crouching with his head down, one in yellow and one in pale grey turned away, and in the middle of them a quiet dark haired figure in rose seated upright and unafraid, a far dim shore showing through the murk at the right, and the green black water heaving right across the bottom of the picture, in the world you will have tribulation, but take courage, i have overcome the world, …
pictures.name: pd_bakhuizen_christ_in_the_storm_on_the_sea_of_galilee

lines.text: I have told you these things so that you will not fall away. They will put you out of the synagogues. In fact, a time is coming when anyone who kills you will think he is offering a service to God.
They will do these things because they have not known the Father or Me.
But I have told you these things so that when their hour comes, you will remember that I told you about them. I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.
Now, however, I am going to Him who sent Me; yet none of you asks Me, Where are You going?
Instead, your hearts are filled with sorrow because I have told you these things.
But I tell you the truth, it is for your benefit that I am going away. Unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send Him to you.
And when He comes, He will convict the world in regard to sin and righteousness and judgment:
in regard to sin, because they do not believe in Me;
in regard to righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will no longer see Me;
and in regard to judgment, because the prince of this world has been condemned.
I still have much to tell you, but you cannot yet bear to hear it.
However, when the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all truth. For He will not speak on His own, but He will speak what He hears, and He will declare to you what is to come.
He will glorify Me by taking from what is Mine and disclosing it to you.
Everything that belongs to the Father is Mine. That is why I said that the Spirit will take from what is Mine and disclose it to you.
In a little while you will see Me no more, and then after a little while you will see Me.
Then some of His disciples asked one another, Why is He telling us, In a little while you will not see Me, and then after a little while you will see Me and Because I am going to the Father?
They kept asking, Why is He saying, a little while? We do not understand what He is saying.
Aware that they wanted to question Him, Jesus said to them, Are you asking one another why I said, In a little while you will not see Me, and then after a little while you will see Me?
Truly, truly, I tell you, you will weep and wail while the world rejoices. You will grieve, but your grief will turn to joy.
A woman has pain in childbirth because her time has come; but when she brings forth her child, she forgets her anguish because of her joy that a child has been born into the world.
So also you have sorrow now, but I will see you again and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy.
In that day you will no longer ask Me anything. Truly, truly, I tell you, whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
Until now you have not asked for anything in My name. Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.
I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you this way, but will tell you plainly about the Father.
In that day you will ask in My name. I am not saying that I will ask the Father on your behalf.
For the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me and have believed that I came from God.
I came from the Father and entered the world. In turn, I will leave the world and go to the Father.
His disciples said, See, now You are speaking plainly and without figures of speech.
Now we understand that You know all things and that You have no need for anyone to question You. Because of this, we believe that You came from God.
Do you finally believe? Jesus replied.
Look, an hour is coming and has already come when you will be scattered, each to his own home, and you will leave Me all alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.
I have told you these things so that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation. But take courage; I have overcome the world!
